Check that every cell has enough persons

check_min_count.Rd

Works on microdata (one row per person or observation, give by) and on aggregated tables (one row per cell, with a count column). Empty cells (0) are allowed; cells with between 1 and min_count - 1 persons fail.

Usage

check_min_count(
  x,
  by = NULL,
  count = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  config = NULL,
  target = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame, or a table/matrix of counts.

by

Grouping variables. For an aggregated table the default is all non-numeric columns.

count

Name of the count column in an aggregated table. Detected automatically when a column is called n, count, freq or similar. Leave NULL with by for microdata.

id

Person identifier in microdata. Persons, not rows, are counted. Without id each row is one person.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

target

Label used in reports.

Value

A mimic_check. details lists the failing groups by label, never their counts.

See also

Other checks: check_differencing(), check_dominance(), check_extremes(), check_group_disclosure(), check_k_anonymity(), check_keys(), check_model(), check_suppression()

Examples

check_min_count(fake_persons, by = "settlement", id = "person_id")
#> ✖ min_count (fake_persons): 5 of 22 cells have fewer than 5 persons.
#>     settlement
#>  Settlement_17
#>  Settlement_16
#>  Settlement_19
#>  Settlement_18
#>  Settlement_20

tab <- as.data.frame(table(sex = fake_persons$sex))
check_min_count(tab)
#> ✔ min_count (tab): All 2 cells have 0 or at least 5 persons.
